newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower on yen, auto stock woes.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower on yen, auto stock woes.

text.p: Weakness in automotive-related stocks helped pull Malaysia's blue chip index to a lower close on Tuesday, analysts said.
At the close, the benchmark Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks dropped 3.97 points to 1,084.55, while the broader EMAS index shed 1.75 points to 309.73.

"The strength of the yen is making investors worried that this marks the beginning of a trend, linked to the recovery in the Japanese economy," said Soh Meng Hui, head of research at K.L. City Securities.
Volume remained thin, with 148 million shares traded.
Hicom Holdings, which controls national car maker Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional (Proton), lost seven cents to 4.98. Proton fell 10 cents to 13.50 ringgit.
Proton cars have a large percentage of components that are made in Japan, while the Hicom group of companies also imports and distributes Japanese four-wheel-drive vehicles.
The Japanese yen has appreciated around six percent over the last week, causing fears that the rise may damage earnings of auto-related companies.
UMW Holdings was down 70 cents to 11.70, while Gadek lost 70 cents to 13.80.
